role: industry association issuing noise/vibration design guidelines for rapid transit facilities
stance_basis: cited as authoritative design guidelines source for noise/vibration criteria without expressing a position on the project
summary: The American Public Transit Association (APTA) is referenced in the document solely as the source of noise and vibration design guidelines used to evaluate and govern the Buffalo Metrorail system. Its guidelines are cited to establish acceptable noise levels for wayside operations, station areas, ancillary facilities, and service yards. APTA takes no position on the project itself; it functions as a technical standards authority whose criteria the project is designed to meet.
complaint_summary: The document cites APTA Design Guidelines to classify all three alternative service yard sites as Category 4, under which peak noise levels of 85 dBA at the yard perimeter would be acceptable and there would be no restriction on ground-borne noise levels.
summary_quote: American Public Transit Association Guidelines (August 1976). GUIDELINES AND PRINCIPLES FOR DESIGN OF RAPID TRANSIT FACILITIES NOISE AND VIBRATION

mentions.quote: The American Public Transit Association guidelines used for design purposes recommend that the single event maximum noise level should be used for design purposes rather than any of the 'noise exposure level' evaluation schemes (Appendix, paragraph 7.1).
mentions.role_as_written: Industry standards body providing design guidelines

mentions.quote: The APTA ground-borne noise guideline of 30 dBA is appropriate for the War Memorial Auditorium and St. Paul's Cathedral.
